claim:
For every integer \(d\ge 1\) and every integer \(h\ge 2\), let \(F(z)=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d}c_\varepsilon z^\varepsilon\) on normalized Haar \(\mathbb T^d\). Then
\[
\|F\|_{L^{2h}(\mathbb T^d)}^{2h}\le \left(2^{-h}\binom{2h}{h}\right)^d\left(\sum_\varepsilon |c_\varepsilon|^2\right)^h.
\]
The constant is sharp, so \(K_{2h}(\{0,1\}^d)=\left(2^{-h}\binom{2h}{h}\right)^{d/(2h)}\). For a nonzero coefficient family, equality holds if and only if there are \(\lambda\ne0\) and phases \(|\eta_j|=1\) such that \(c_\varepsilon=\lambda\prod_{j=1}^d\eta_j^{\varepsilon_j}\); equivalently, \(F(z)=\lambda\prod_{j=1}^d(1+\eta_jz_j)\).
integrity: The proof is analytic for all stated dimensions and even exponents. Finite exact computations only corroborate identities and examples and are not used as exhaustive evidence for the infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The proof is for even exponents and the Cartesian two-character spectrum. It does not determine non-even sharp constants or arbitrary finite spectra. An older equivalent tensor-product formulation could remain bibliographically unlocated.
title: Exact even-moment constants of the Boolean rectangular spectrum
